# RLS Doctor

Don't trust your RLS. Prove it. Read-only Postgres and Supabase Row Level Security audit with a rolled-back probe that proves cross-tenant reads.

## What it does

Reads catalog metadata and reports RLS risks: disabled RLS on granted tables, unconditional `using (true)` policies, missing `WITH CHECK`, reachable `TRUNCATE`, disabled `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and broad default privileges. `probe` impersonates application roles in a rolled-back read-only transaction and shows which rows they can actually read. `check --schema-file <path>` audits a SQL migration offline with no database. Every report carries a deterministic RLS Score (`--score`, `--badge`).

## Install

```bash
npx rls-doctor check
```

## One command

```bash
rls-doctor check                                    # catalog audit
rls-doctor explain public.profiles                  # one table
rls-doctor probe --app-roles authenticated          # behavioral proof
rls-doctor demo                                     # disposable Postgres, proven leak
```

## What it does not do

It never mutates the database. Probe runs inside a rolled-back transaction. It does not call Supabase management APIs and cannot see application-level authorization bugs.

## Limits

Catalog analysis cannot prove runtime authz. Probe results depend on seeded data — empty tables prove nothing.

## For agents

- Skill: `.agents/skills/rls-doctor/SKILL.md` (also `.claude/skills/` after `npx skills add subhajitlucky/rls-doctor`)
- MCP: `claude mcp add rls-doctor --scope user -- npx -y rls-doctor@0.5.8 mcp` — tools: `describe_capabilities`, `check_rls`, `probe_access`, `explain_table`, `prove_isolation`, `propose_repair` (all read-only, annotated)
- MCP errors: `{ error: { code, message, nextAction } }` — branch on `code`, not prose
- Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` findings at/above `--fail-on`, `2` operational failure (never clean)
- Other clients (Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, generic stdio): https://github.com/subhajitlucky/rls-doctor/blob/main/docs/agents.md
